title: Decide whether the hub signs a hash-chain entry alongside the fanout sequence
description:
docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §7.1 and §12.4, which until now cited bead
mimid-1wgh.37.104.1 for this. That bead is closed and carried a
different question: where the sequence rides in the /notify envelope,
answered by the mimi-fanout-sequence header. The hash-chain question
was never its subject and has had no bead of its own.

THE QUESTION. Nothing in the design binds a sequence to a message in a
way a third party can check. Franking covers hub acceptance where it
applies; the sequence is an HTTP header covered only by the RFC 9421
signature on the request that carried it, so a holder that is not the
hub can renumber, reorder or omit without the receiver noticing.
Should the hub sign a running hash over the room's fanout stream -- an
entry over (previous, sequence, message digest) -- assigned in the same
place and at the same time as the sequence?

THE TWO READINGS.

1. Assign it now, beside the sequence (§4). Any holder can then prove a
message's position and no holder can hide a gap. It costs a signature
and a chain entry per fanout, and a second thing in the envelope for
every implementation that parses it.
2. Leave it to peer-to-peer backlog (bead mimid-1wgh.37.105), where it
is question 2 of that design and where the need for it arises. It
costs a retrofit: the envelope, draft-atwood-mimi-catchup (bead
mimid-1wgh.37.104.13) and any protocol-08 text (bead
mimid-1wgh.37.104.15) would all change once other implementations
parse them.

WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT ON mimid-1wgh.37.105. §7.1 says the addition is
to this design and not only to §7's, and the timing is what makes it a
question: mimid-1wgh.37.105 is P3, not started, and blocked on its own
question 1 (whether a follower may serve a room's fanout to another
follower at all), so parking the chain entry there decides reading 2 by
default. mimid-1wgh.37.105 question 2 states the same mechanism and
says to consider assigning it with the sequence; this bead is that
consideration, and the two are one answer.

Mark's to answer. No code until it is answered.
